title: Western Conference Contender Not Pursuing Giannis Antetokounmpo Despite Having Exactly What The Bucks Desire - NewsBreak
text:
By Kenny Nosay ,
1 hours ago
Giannis Antetokounmpo (Image Credits: Imagn) Many pundits aren’t positive of the Milwaukee Bucks’ chances for a title this upcoming season. Most of the reason is due to their lack of roster depth surrounding Giannis Antetokounmpo . As we all know by now, Damian Lillard is back with Portland. Long-time center Brook Lopez is gone. If we deduct Antetokounmpo from the equation, the team’s roster construction looks like it’s rebuilding.
At 31 years old, it’s understandable for the former two-time MVP to drop hints about his future with the team. The rumor mill has started to ramp up this offseason about his impending departure. However, not all teams have the right assets to trade for a superstar like Giannis Antetokounmpo.
The Oklahoma City Thunder, which has a wealth of tradable assets, including future picks and players, is reportedly not interested in acquiring Giannis via trade this season, according to a report from Chris Mannix of Sports Illustrated.
As their roster is currently constructed, it’s quite logical for OKC not to vie for the services of Giannis. The team already has two superstars in Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jalen Williams. They just won a championship in 2025. They are young and building a dynasty. Antetokounmpo has no place on their team for the time being.
Bucks Prefer Future Assets For A Giannis Antetokounmpo Trade Giannis Antetokounmpo (Image Credits: Imagn) With the Bucks not having any control of any of their draft picks until 2031, it’s logical that they would prefer receiving a boatload of picks for Giannis in any trade . They see his impending departure as the start of their rebuilding phase. Quite frankly, that’s the right approach to take in this scenario.
It generally seems like Antetokounmpo’s time with the Bucks is numbered. While Giannis hasn’t explicitly said that he’s unhappy with the organization, he just wants to compete for more championships now that he’s in his 30s.
